display.purpose: Hero SHREY PATEL wordmark morph only — appears once per page load.

headline.purpose: Section/app logotypes, e.g. the About.exe badge, at reduced Chakra Petch scale.

title.purpose: Window and card titles, System Properties identity text.

label.purpose: Chrome text — menu items, taskbar labels, spec rows, tray text.

micro-body.purpose: Section-head captions and prose sized just under the Body floor — its own step, between Label and Body.

mono.purpose: Terminal panes, boot sequences, status bars — anything reading as the machine talking.

shadows.name: sunken-well
shadows.purpose: Recessed-fieldset / pressed-field glow, paired with the reversed bevel border.

shadows.name: signature-glow-light
shadows.purpose: Focus/active glow using the light-theme signature color.

shadows.name: signature-glow-dark
shadows.purpose: Focus/active glow using the dark-theme signature color.

shadows.name: crt-vignette
shadows.purpose: Screen-edge darkening on CRT/monitor-framed surfaces only.

shadows.name: floating-window
shadows.purpose: Real elevation for draggable/floating windows over the desktop, stacked on the raised bevel border. The one sanctioned exception to bevel-only depth; reserved for floating windows, never static cards.

motion.name: ease-window
motion.purpose: Default easing for window open/drag/minimize transitions.

components.name: Chrome Button
components.description: Raised bevel button used for Start button, taskbar task buttons, window control buttons.
components.css: .ds-btn-chrome { height: 24px; padding: 0 8px; background: var(--chrome, #c0c0c0); color: #000; font-family: var(--f-sys, 'IBM Plex Sans', sans-serif); font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; border: 2px solid; border-top-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); border-left-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); border-right-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-bottom-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-radius: 0; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-chrome:active, .ds-btn-chrome.ds-active { border-top-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-left-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-right-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); border-bottom-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); } .ds-btn-chrome:focus-visible { outline: 2px dotted #fff; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Close Button
components.description: Window titlebar close control — the one button allowed a non-bevel hover treatment (destructive signal).
components.css: .ds-btn-close { width: 16px; height: 14px; background: var(--chrome, #c0c0c0); color: #000; font-size: 9px; border: 1.5px solid; border-top-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); border-left-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); border-right-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-bottom-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-radius: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-close:hover { background: #c0392b; color: #fff; } .ds-btn-close:active { border-top-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-left-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-right-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); border-bottom-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); }

components.name: Window Panel
components.description: Full window chrome: navy/amber titlebar gradient over a silver bevel-bordered panel body.
components.css: .ds-window { background: var(--win-face, #c0c0c0); border: 2px solid; border-top-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); border-left-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); border-right-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-bottom-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-radius: 0; } .ds-window-title { height: 22px; display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 0 6px; background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--tb-start, #000080), var(--tb-end, #1084d0)); color: #fff; font-family: var(--f-sys, 'IBM Plex Sans', sans-serif); font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; } .ds-window-body { padding: 12px; font-family: var(--f-sys, 'IBM Plex Sans', sans-serif); font-size: 13px; color: var(--win-text, #000); }

components.name: Sunken Field
components.description: Pre-inverted bevel well — the single shared recipe for text fields, trays, and meters.
components.css: .ds-field-sunken { height: 24px; padding: 0 7px; background: var(--field-bg, #fff); color: var(--field-text, #000); font-family: var(--f-mono, 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace); font-size: 13px; border: 1.5px solid; border-top-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-left-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-right-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); border-bottom-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); border-radius: 0; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.15); } .ds-field-sunken:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #e89020); outline-offset: -2px; }

components.name: Taskbar Task Button
components.description: Open-window entry in the taskbar; pressed/inverted bevel signals the active window.
components.css: .ds-tb-task { height: 24px; max-width: 172px; padding: 0 8px; background: var(--chrome, #c0c0c0); color: #000; font-family: var(--f-sys, 'IBM Plex Sans', sans-serif); font-size: 11px; border: 2px solid; border-top-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); border-left-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); border-right-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-bottom-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-radius: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tb-task-active { border-top-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-left-color: var(--chrome-dk, #808080); border-right-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); border-bottom-color: var(--chrome-lt, #dfdfdf); }

narrative.overview: SHREY/OS is not a retro-themed website — it is a Windows 95/98-era desktop that happens to run in a browser and happens to be a portfolio. Every window drags, every button depresses, every boot sequence actually boots. The chrome is authentic down to the 1px bevel, but nothing about it is inert set-dressing: the CRT boot, the dial-up handshake, the BSOD, the screensaver are all wired to real application state (OSContext), not looping video. The system's entire claim to craft rests on this distinction — a themed React site could copy the beige and the scanlines; it could not copy a taskbar that actually tracks open windows. Two hard rejections keep this honest: no flat modern SaaS surface (soft rounded corners, ambient gradients, floating cards) is allowed to leak in anywhere, and no section is allowed to invent its own visual identity — the OS is one continuous machine, not a set of themed pages wearing a shared header.
keyCharacteristics: Hard 1–2px bevel borders (light top/left, dark bottom/right) are the only depth language for controls; soft shadows are reserved for a handful of cinematic/CRT moments, never for ordinary chrome.
One signature accent pair — Windows Navy in light mode, Terminal Amber in dark — is reused verbatim by every section.
Sharp corners everywhere except literal circular controls and the toggle switch.
Type is real web fonts standing in for period system faces so mobile never falls back to a different platform font than desktop.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Every section's signature color is the same navy/amber pair, never a per-section hue. A section is allowed its own supporting palette but never its own primary identity color.

rules.name: The Bevel-Only Rule
rules.body: Depth on any interactive control comes from a 1–2px hard-edged bevel, never from border-radius + soft shadow. Soft shadow is reserved for CRT/cinematic effects only.

rules.name: The One Wordmark Rule
rules.body: Chakra Petch is reserved for logotype-scale moments. It never appears in body copy, buttons, or chrome.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Elevation appears only via the bevel-border pair, or a glow that responds to state, never as ambient decoration on a static element.

dos: Do build depth with the bevel-border pair (raised: light top/left, dark bottom/right; sunken: reversed) on every interactive control.
Do reuse the exact Windows Navy (#000080) / Terminal Amber (#ffb454) pair for any new section's signature identity — never introduce a new per-section hue.
Do keep corners sharp (0px radius) on all chrome, windows, buttons, and fields; reserve rounding for literal circles and the one toggle-switch pill.
Do keep Chakra Petch scarce — logotype scale only — so IBM Plex Sans/Mono carry everything else as one coherent chrome voice.
donts: Don't introduce soft ambient shadows, rounded-corner cards, or gradient-mesh backgrounds anywhere — that is the explicitly rejected flat-modern-SaaS look.
Don't give a section its own accent hue distinct from the shared navy/amber signature pair.
Don't mix the bevel and soft-shadow depth languages on the same element.
Don't set data-theme from inside a section component — it's owned exclusively by OSContext and written once on <html>.
